technology.summary: Today's technology news includes a warning from a top House Democrat that Chinese AI companies could cause havoc on the world. This comes as Anthropic, an AI company, warns of 'catastrophic' AI risks in its IPO filing, while OpenAI says it won't go public until its models are safe. Meanwhile, Peak XV has unveiled an 18-startup cohort, and Reco has raised $55 million as AI agent security startups crowd the market.

Peak XV ups Surge seed investment ceiling to $5M, unveils 18-startup cohort
Reco raises $55M as AI agent security startups crowd the market

finance.summary: Today's most important finance news includes the MSCI Asia Pacific Index climbing 0.6% with stocks in Japan and South Korea gaining, and the Shapoorji Pallonji Group planning to generate $125 million through a tap issue of current dollar bonds. The Nifty 50 saw a drop of 64.05 points, or 0.28%, closing at 22,716.20, and KPIT Technologies faces a substantial 24% decline in stock value. Legacy fund houses outperformed newer asset management companies in four of six categories.

politics.summary:
The Maharashtra Government has unveiled a Fodder Development Policy to tackle a shortage. The policy will include a list of suitable grasses for cultivation, fodder-producing trees, improved fodder crops, and traditional and non-traditional sources of fodder.

In other news, the Bombay High Court will hear a plea seeking transparency in Maharashtra SIR, which could result in the deletion of 2.1 crore names from the electoral rolls in the State.

The Kerala High Court has directed transparency in the selection of Sabarimala and Malikappuram Melsanthis.

The BJP president has told West Bengal BJP ministers that the party should not interfere in government functioning.
